doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Signing Joe Williams, Dakota Staton and Nancy Wilson
summary: Joe Williams phones after leaving Basie with no contract; other clients come through Capitol Records and Cannonball.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: business. And then one by one different people came along. And I knew Joe, for years I’d known Joe Williams. And when he left the Basie band and he called me one day he said, “come and take this telephone out of my hands.”

And that was it. No contract. No nothing. And the other people I guess came along through the record companies. In those days, especially Capitol Records, almost anybody who was anybody that came through the label that didn’t have management I’d get a call and they’d say — in jazz that is, you know — “do you want to manage this person?” Or they’d recommend me, you know. And that way I remember Dakota Staton was one. She was on Capitol Records and Dave Cavanaugh, who was the A&R man for George Shearing and later on for Cannonball and everybody. So a lot of the people that I had at that time was on the Capitol label. Nancy Wilson came along through that. Through Cannonball I met Nancy, and it just went from one to the other. And all of a sudden I found myself—
Somebody take the phone out of your hands—
